options: Linear maps are defined only on finite sets.

questions.skill_detail: conceptual: Key result: a linear map is completely determined by its values on a basis.
option_explanations: Linear maps are not restricted to finite sets.
Basis vectors may map to any vectors, and those images determine the whole map by linearity; e.g. $T(e_1)=(1,0)$, $T(e_2)=(0,1)$ defines the identity map, not the zero map.

A linear map is defined on the entire domain, not only the basis: once $Ae_i$ is known, every $v=\sum_i c_ie_i$ is sent to $Av=\sum_i c_iAe_i$ by additivity and homogeneity, so vectors outside the basis are still mapped via their expansion.
